text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Accountancy groups Arthur Andersen and Price Waterhouse clash with Dutch Bar Association over right to move into legal services sector. (p1)
- Retail sector turnover in the Netherlands grows by 3.2 pct in 1996, the highest growth in five years. (p1)
- Rotterdam court rules that bulk terminal EBS can force 276 of its 650 employees to leave. (p1)
- Small majority of staff of Belgian steel company Boel agrees to Dutch steel maker Hoogovens' social plan arranging a cut of 800 of the 2100 jobs. (p1)
- Parliament to ask junior finance minister for information on tax loss resulting from fiscal arrangement between Philips Electronics, Rabobank and tax office in 1993. (p3)
- Fight for control of AIR Holding ends as J&J Investments places its AIR stake in the hands of investors. (p3)
- Sweets maker Klene's 1996 net profit grows faster than expected, by 12 percent to Dfl 2.2 million. (p4)
- Publisher Reed Elsevier sells the trade division of Reed Books to U.S. publisher Random House. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Broadcaster NOS buys premier soccer league TV rights for 35 million guilders. (p1)
- Social affairs minister Ad Melkert does not allow his civil servants to participate in a public debate in parliament on social benefits. (p11)
- Strikes threaten at Hoogovens as talks between unions and the steel maker's management grind to a halt. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- ABN AMRO to finance oil exploration in east coast Russian peninsular Sakhalin. (p11)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Container transhipment company ECT invests 40 million guilders in four cranes. (p11)
- Conflict at HES Beheer's dry bulk unit EBS hardens as management threatens a shake-out of jobs. (p119
TROUW
- Amsterdam bewildered by nature conservationists' refusal to stop referendum after environment minister's decision to limit residential area on artificial islands to 18,000 houses. (p1)
- A group of medium-sized transport companies leave sector organisation TLN to found new organisation WN. (p3)
